title: Fats writes 'Ain't Misbehavin'' and other hits in jail over alimony
summary: Autrey says Fats wrote 'Ain't Misbehavin'', 'My Fate Is in Your Hands' and 'Keepin' Out of Mischief Now' while jailed for alimony, with Andy Razaf and J. C. Johnson as lyricists.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That -- well you know about his 'Ain't Misbehavin'' and all that stuff. Did you hear the story about that?
No, what's the story on that?
He wrote that in jail!
He did?

Yeah, she had him locked up for alimony, you know, and he wrote 'Ain't misbehavin', blah-dah doo doo. All by myself, deedle doodle doo, I used to sing the damn thing, Ain't misbehavin' saving my love for you. Hear me
talking to you. I know for certain, you're the one I love. I'm through with flirting, baby, it's you that I'm thinking of. Ain't misbehavin' saving all my love for you.
He was in the hospital -- hospital, -- he was in jail when he wrote this --
Didn't Andy Razof write the words?
Yeah, right, Andy wrote that.
Fats wrote the tune.

Andy Razof and J. C. Johnson. They collaborated. They did a lot of those things. So he was trying to make it lighter on himself for -- you know, give him a break. And then he wrote -- another thing he wrote while he was in there, 'My Fate's in Your Hands.'
Wasn't 'Keeping Out of Mischief' one of the --
'Keeping Out of -- yeah. Keeping (sings) Out of Mischief, dah --
These were all while he was in jail?
Huh?
This was all while --
In jail, yeah. Man, he wrote these tunes in jail, The love that cannot be. all of them came out to be hits.
How long was he in jail?
He told me. How the hell long was he
in there? How many months? I don't remember.
Oh, months? It wasn't just a few days, or --

Well, I mean it was -- you know for alimony, you know how those things can go. He told me. I've forgotten now. I'm trying to think of some of the other things he wrote while he was in jail. Hmmm, hmmm, hmmm, You're my judge and jury, dah dah dah dah doo dah.
'My Fate is In Your Hands.' That's the one, yeah.
